Both rulings found the right declarations and both ruled OK; the adjudication rule is sharper than either used. Clause (i) is stated twice over — TerminalEdgeFactor.lean:1631 in backward-stress form, with fewer hypotheses than the paper (arbitrary C, d, y0; only y.2 ≤ 0), and LeadingStressWeights.lean:431 in axis-stress form for the modulated family. That is lean_weaker, hence DELTA — low severity, since the field the paper carries forward is covered and no downstream use of the general form was found.

findings.summary: Clause (ii), and clause (i) in its axis-stress form, are stated only for constructed witness families, not for an arbitrary field assumed to satisfy the moment conditions. Clause (i) in backward-stress form is stated with fewer hypotheses than the paper.

The two representation theorems carry the strict hypothesis 1/2 < y where the paper asserts y \ge 1/2. The endpoint is recovered only on the normalized section q = 1; at a general physical point with y = 1/2 it is not stated.
The axial half of (A.46) is written over s = r^2/2 (axialBackwardStress) rather than over r, so the two statements agree only after a change of variable.
